scenes.title:
Documentation
from the model
scenes.subtitle: The architecture document, generated from the model the system comes from.

narration.en: Tickets, from episode five: four contexts, five apps, two external systems. One command, hla, writes its architecture document to a single file, next to the pom.
It is Markdown. The objective is the one written in the model. The diagrams are Mermaid: plain text, so when the document changes, the change reads in a diff, like code.

Rendered, with its diagrams drawn, the structural view. Each service, with its bounded context. The apps. The external systems. And between Sales and Payments, the relations and the events they exchange.

Then, context by context: the aggregates, with their fields, and the use cases, each one described by the intent written in the model. Where the model says nothing, the document shows a dash. It never makes anything up.

A state diagram for each aggregate with a lifecycle. And the cross-cutting concerns, read from the flags in the model. Sales and Payments use an outbox. Catalog publishes directly, and the document says what that risks.
Then what the system exposes: each app with its menu, each API with its operations. And last, the open points: the decisions still proposed.
So the team decides. The decision goes into the model, as one more file. And Catalog's service turns its outbox on.
The decision is in the table. The outbox line now names Catalog. Nobody edited the document: it followed the model.

scenes.caption: The same model, the same change.

narration.en: And generate takes the same change to the code: Catalog gets an outbox, its relay, and a migration for its table.

scenes.title:
One model.
The system, and its documentation.

narration.en: The code and the architecture document come from the same model. When the model changes, run hla again, and review the document's diff like any other.
